g.text: Figure 8b | Archived factors improve population-wide held-out reconstruction

text.style: font-size: 8.6px; font-family: 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', 'Computer Modern Sans Serif', 'Lucida Grande', 'Verdana', 'Geneva', 'Lucid', 'Avant Garde', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #56616f

g.text: A broken y-axis enlarges the central distributions while retaining every neuron's high-R² tail; diamonds are medians.

text.style: font-size: 6.7px; font-family: 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', 'Computer Modern Sans Serif', 'Lucida Grande', 'Verdana', 'Geneva', 'Lucid', 'Avant Garde', sans-serif; fill: #4f5964

g.text: Every one of the 603 strict-QC neurons contributes a complete-trial out-of-fold R² for the mean-rate, cue-PSTH, event-time-PSTH and archived-factor downstream readouts. The full

text.style: font-size: 6.7px; font-family: 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', 'Computer Modern Sans Serif', 'Lucida Grande', 'Verdana', 'Geneva', 'Lucid', 'Avant Garde', sans-serif; fill: #4f5964

g.text: untrimmed values are plotted on both axis segments. Absolute spike-level R² remains modest even though the archived-factor median exceeds the template baselines.
